label: D1 before an upcoming a1 choice, unless the last trial ended in S2
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), when the agent is about to choose a1 and the previous trial did not end in S2 (in practice: the last trial was a1 to S1 via a common transition, or it is the first trial of the window). The upcoming choice is the agent own policy output, so this counts as observed and not future; the model policy logit at D1 (choice > 0 with prev_state != 2) gives a similar dev F1 of 0.91. Without the upcoming-choice term, the purely past predicate D1 & prev_action==1 & prev_state==1 has precision 0.96 but recall 0.76, because it misses window-first trials where the history is unknown. Activity is much higher when the previous reward was shown (in_rew=1: 41% active, 78% of mass). From the example windows (not measured with a score), magnitude appears to build over consecutive rewarded a1 to S1 trials and peaks on the D1 right after such a run. It does not fire after a2 choices, after rare a1 to S2 transitions, before upcoming a2 choices, or outside D1. Dev F1 0.90, mass recall 0.95.

issues: Phase claims check out. The feature fires only at D1 (34% of D1 steps active, 0 at GO and 0 at D2), and almost never after the previous trial reached S2 (D1 & prev_action==1 & prev_state==2 has precision 0.006).

The claim that it does not fire before an upcoming a2 choice is false. After a common a1->S1 trial it fires before an upcoming a2 at about the same rate as before a1: D1 & action==2 & prev_action==1 & prev_state==1 has precision 0.890 on dev (n=6846) and 0.889 on test (n=8145). The predicate's action==1 term wrongly excludes these steps, so the upcoming choice is not what drives the feature.

'Unless the last trial ended in S2' is the wrong condition. The predicate counts rare a2->S1 trials as positives, but the feature mostly stays silent there: D1 & action==1 & prev_action==2 & prev_state==1 has precision 0.254 on dev (n=4347) and 0.230 on test (n=5354). What matters is that the previous trial was a common a1->S1 trial, not just that it did not end in S2.

The upcoming-action term only helps on the window's first trial (rel -3), where prev_* is unknown in the variables even though the GRU has seen that history. There, action==1 is just a proxy for the unseen previous trial, with precision 0.739. Using only the past, D1 & prev_action==1 & prev_state==1 already has precision 0.950 on test.

A better predicate that drops the false action conditioning beats the original on test: F1 0.923 vs 0.888, mass recall 0.983 vs 0.946. The same predicate with the policy logit (choice>0) in place of action on first trials scores test F1 0.919.

The claim that magnitude builds over a run of rewarded trials was never scored. The feature also fires after unrewarded common a1->S1 trials: precision 0.987 with action==1, and 0.959 for D1 & prev_action==1 & prev_state==1 & prev_reward==0. So reward raises how often it fires but is not required.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 right after a common a1->S1 trial (rewarded or not), whatever the upcoming choice; on the window's first trial, where that history is unknown, the upcoming a1 choice stands in for it
